notes: SOURCE: nigh-perfect replica of Earth; you awaken in your pre-Backrooms home; inconsistencies grow with time (lamp posts too tall, sound lagging behind its cause, animals at ~100 m briefly lacking or having excess skin, almond water unknown to vendors and search engines, New Zealand on no map); no outposts; entered via unlocked doors in Level 2; saying "I'm ready to go back" -> unconscious -> Level 0. TESTIMONY (narrative frame): windy cold beach, sand and shells, quiet despite the sea, a smooth purple-white shell, waves out of sync with their sound, sun a little too far left, clouds a fraction too fast, being asked to head in. ADAPTATION: 'your home' is a generic two-storey seaside house (hall with stair, living room, kitchen, study, dining room; bedroom, bathroom, spare room of unpacked boxes) on a street of closed neighbours' houses whose gardens run to a dune and the narrative's beach; no family or people are shown (canon trap: the family is narrative); the street streams along X in 48 m chunks (finite window); wrongness rises over ~15 minutes: street lamps stretch up to ~1.85x, the swash's crash sound lags up to 1.7 s, the sun drifts 16 degrees left and clouds speed up 4x, a distant gull flickers to a baggy-skinned mesh for 0.35 s; the return phrase is offered at the bed, the back deck and the shore (all one edge); the world map is a procedural sketch without New Zealand. The DEV26 overlay cues (book, coat rack, cup) are re-homed onto matching furniture at runtime and their glow markers hidden.
entity_policy: NO ENTITY PER SOURCE. No people are modelled: the family belongs to the narrative. Gulls are ordinary animals of the Earth replica; their 'wrong skin' is a momentary hallucination (SOURCE). Hounds, fires and faceless things are memories in the narrative and never appear.
